Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The issue reported relates to the implementation of the HW rule in the Soundex algorithm. The HW rule states that if two characters mapping to the same code are separated by an 'H' or 'W', the second character should not be encoded.

Looking at the code of Soundex.getMappingCode(String, int), it checks if the index is greater than 1 and the mapped character is not '0'. It then checks if the character before the current one is 'H' or 'W'. If so, it further inspects the character two places before (index-2). It maps this character and compares its code with the current mapped character.

If this preceding character's code is the same as the current mapped character OR if the preceding character itself is 'H' or 'W', the method returns 0, indicating not to encode the character at the current index.

The bug is due to the condition in the line:
```java
if (firstCode == mappedChar || 'H' == preHWChar || 'W' == preHWChar) {
    return 0;
}
```
This condition causes a character to be ignored (return 0) not only when it is separated by an 'H' or 'W' and the preceding consonant shares the same code, but also incorrectly when the preceding character itself is 'H' or 'W' regardless of what the first consonant was.

Therefore, the method erroneously disallows encoding even when the HW letters are repeated or when the preceding character was not a consonant matching the current one. This deviates from the official Soundex HW rule, causing incorrect encoding results such as the failure seen with inputs like "Ashcraft".

In summary, the bug arises because the check:
```java
' H' == preHWChar || 'W' == preHWChar
```
should not cause returning 0 unconditionally. Only the case where the firstCode equals the current mapped code should suppress encoding. The current logic is too broad and causes over-suppression, leading to the bug described.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
